So, while I was in training at Sandhill I was selected to be assigned to the 3rd US INF REGT (The Old Guard) one of the only two free standing regiments left in the Army. Those of you who may not know The Old Guard is a double duty Infantry unit. During peacetime we perform all the funerals at Arlington National Cemetery, White House Ceremonies, Retirement Ceremonies, etc. Our unit is also tasked with being the defense unit of the capitol, so we have a very busy schedule that rotates between ceremonies and tactical training. Due to this Infantrymen are hand selected from all trainees at 30th AG (fucking hellhole). So, we are picked for height, build, no major facial scars, your last PT test in Basic has to be above 70 in all events, and you have to have at least a 110 GT score from your ASVAB. Now enters our heroic protagonist, Pitt (not real name). The dumbest mother fucker I have ever seen wear a uniform. Now, the amount of stupidity that fell out of this kid created so many events they are hard to remember them all (Plus we are talking almost 12 years, so memory fades), but these three major things stand out above the rest. First major thing was when standing at attention he could form his hand into a "C" fist properly. Like the concept itself escaped him. You literally just have to imagine you are holding a bucket by the wire handle and your hand does the rest. Well, everyone struggled so hard to get the concept through to him that his Team Leader finally taped his hand in the position for hours at a time hoping the muscle memory would take over to no avail. Earning him the nickname Old Guard Pitt as a slight. The next major event happened memorial day weekend. Pitt and his team leader Williams (real last name, but it is so common in the Army might as well be Smith). So, I'm in the off post room with Williams and we are both preparing our blues for funerals the next day when the phone rings. He reaches down and hits the speaker button " Sergeant Williams" "Sergeant, the general is here to see you'" Comes Pitt's half sleepy tone. "I'm a Colonel." Comes the Regimental Commander's voice behind his. Williams and I just exchange an are you fucking kidding me look, and Williams changes into a sly grin. "Pitt, who did you say is here?" Williams asked. "The General, Sergeant, he came to talk to you," Pitt replied. "I JUST TOLD YOU I'M A COLONEL!" came our Commander's response. "Alright, be right down." Williams hung the phone up and said " I better get down there, hahaha!" From that day on Pitt had to walk around with rank flash cards in his left chest pocket. And here is the crescendo to the epic story that was Old Guard Pitt. One day Williams feeling extra shit heady decides it would be funny to send Pitt to Regimental Headquarters and get the keys to Summerall Field so we can rehearse for a ceremony ( Summerall Field is our parade field and completely open. It is the old grid squares or prop wash gag). Well, Williams failed to remember what time it was or just how stupid Pitt was. So, Pitt heads straight over to Headquarters, and in his infinite wisdom he marches straight past the secretaries and right into the Regimental Training Meeting. There he asked the General Colonel for the keys to Summerall Field in front of CSM and every CO, XO, and 1SG in the Regiment. Resulting in our Command hanging their head in shame while the other commands lost their shit. After the Regiment Headquarters incident our Command had had enough and gave Pitt and Immediate Reassignment to the 25th ID. We felt somewhat bad for a minute till the joy of being rid of him took over.

P.S. Williams lost two weekends to CQ duty for the last one

I got tricked once when I was serving on a submarine. Halfway thru the patrol we had a celebration oddly named halfway day. We had assorted contest's, games, raffles, etc. On my first patrol I was given the esteemed privilege to attempt to qualify to retrieve the "mail buoy" it was said to contain letters,postcards, cookies, presents, and other assorted items from home. We had sporadic emails when not on alert but this supposed treasure trove of delights was going to be delivered by a special helicopter in the middle of the Atlantic in the middle of the night! We were going to swiftly surface the ship in a covert action to meet this Neptune like Santa of the sea! I was going topside alone to get this magical bag for my crew! It was a dark and stormy night and drilling had worn down morale, but I would be the one to pass out pictures of newborn children to fathers who had been away for their birth! Anniversary gifts and championship game copies! I was assured this action would help immensely with signatures for my warfare qualification (which is the most important aspect to serving in the submarine fleet) but also warned that if I lost this mail buoy overboard (its happened before even without a storm!) It would earn much ire and ruin my chances of being part of the ships crew! I had safety gear to wear, and had to seek guidance from all department heads including the XO and CO. I ran around for hours and was waiting all night. Took pictures with everyone. Finally I was informed it was a gag. I felt so stupid. I had some reservations but couldn't believe that all those senior officers were pulling my leg. It did help make me become closer to the crew and gain confidence when dealing with the higher ups.
